want exactly that.
 *
 * ⭐ S6 A8j (2026-10-07) — A FORM WHOSE COMMIT IS THIS DIALOG IS SUBMITTED BY THIS DIALOG ALONE: see `submitsForm`.
 * Enter in such a form opens the dialog, exactly as the trigger does, and never submits the form: before the page
 * wakes, while it hydrates and after. `test:implicit-submit` holds every dialog whose confirm submits a form to the
 * prop and reads the server's markup by each browser engine's own rule; `qa:implicit-submit` presses the keys.
 */

import * as React from "react";

pending?: boolean;
  /**
   * ⭐ S6 A8j (2026-10-07) — THIS DIALOG'S CONFIRM SUBMITS THE FORM ITS TRIGGER SITS IN, AND NOTHING ELSE MAY.
   *
   * 🔴 THE DEFECT IT CLOSES, ON EVERY PLAYER'S WITHDRAWAL. The trigger is forced to `type="button"` (below), which left
   * the withdraw form with no submit button and one text field, and a browser SUBMITS such a form when Enter is pressed
   * in that field (HTML's implicit submission; a phone's Go key is the same Enter). An amount typed and entered left the
   * account with no "Confirm withdrawal" at all: no fee, no "You receive", no recipient. The close-account form was the
   * same shape, and Enter in its phrase box closed the account and its wallet. Before the page woke (its scripts still
   * coming down a slow line) the same Enter posted the server action as plain HTML, which no listener can stop.
   *
   * ⭐ WITH IT ON, ENTER DOES WHAT THE TRIGGER DOES, in three parts, each for a window the others cannot reach:
   *   · THE GUARD (`formGuard`) listens on the form and refuses every submit but the confirm's own, then opens the
   *     dialog by the trigger's own path (its `openGuard`, its `onOpen`), or does nothing where the trigger would do
   *     nothing: disabled, or the dialog already open;
   *   · A DEFAULT BUTTON — a submit button no one sees or reaches, and the form's first, so it is what a browser presses
   *     for Enter — disabled until the guard listens. In Chromium and Firefox a disabled default button stops implicit
   *     submission outright, so the server's markup and the hydration are covered. Once the guard listens it is enabled,
   *     and Enter in ANY field of the form presses it: a submit the guard turns into the dialog (eight fields on the
   *     deposit form, where Enter used to do nothing). `formNoValidate`, so bad input meets the kit's toast and never the
   *     browser's bubble (V-3);
   *   · A SECOND TEXT FIELD, unnamed, unseen and out of reach. WebKit (every browser on an iPhone) skips a disabled
   *     submit button and submits a form of ONE text field anyway; a form of two it submits in no engine.
   * ⛔ The confirm's submit must happen INSIDE `onConfirm` (`requestSubmit()` fires its event before it returns), and
   * the form must hold no submit control of its own: the guard would refuse a later submit as Enter's, and a control of
   * the form's own would be its default button instead. `test:implicit-submit` holds every dialog whose confirm submits
   * a form to this prop.
   */
  submitsForm?: boolean;
};

callsForAli: Pre-hydration is closed too, by server-drawn markup, which goes beyond what A8j asked. Decision: a hidden default submit button, disabled until the guard listens, stops Enter in Chromium and Firefox (most players). A hidden, unnamed second text field stops it in WebKit (every iPhone browser). Why: before the page's scripts run, a server-action form is plain HTML, so Enter posts withdrawAction or closeAccountAction natively and no client listener can stop it. I checked WebKit's source: it skips a disabled submit button and still submits a one-field form, so the finding's 'disabled default button' alone would not protect iPhones. Overrule options: (1) drop the second field and accept that an iPhone can still send a withdrawal with Enter in the seconds before the page wakes; (2) go further and add a server-side seal, where withdrawAction and closeAccountAction refuse a post that didn't come through the confirm. That touches the money actions and needs a refusal sentence in en/sw/zh.

Enter now opens the confirm on the deposit form too; before, Enter there did nothing, because eight text fields stop implicit submission. Decision: one rule for every form whose commit is a ConfirmDialog, 'Enter does what the button does', so deposit's safety no longer rests on its field count. Overrule: keep deposit's Enter doing nothing. That needs a guard-only variant of the prop (no default button) plus a census exemption for deposit.

The hub's sign-out row and the two RG confirms (break, self-exclusion) get submitsForm too, though Enter could never submit them: no text field. Decision: the census rule is the same for every dialog, 'a confirm that submits a form guards it', with no exemptions to rot. Nothing they draw or do changes. Overrule: exempt them by name in the census instead.

Close-account: Enter now does nothing until the phrase is typed, then opens the dialog. It used to post and come back with the 'type the phrase' error. Decision: Enter follows the trigger, which is disabled until the phrase matches. Overrule: show the old message on Enter with an incomplete phrase. That needs a toast with wording in three languages.

Two admin forms are exempted by name, because they save some changes directly by design: GlobalConfigForm (only a money-model change asks) and ReadingMethodForm (only the simulated feed asks). The census pins that each one asks before it saves. Overrule: make either always confirm, and its exemption goes (the census then demands the exemption be deleted).

A ConfirmModal may no longer be wired to submit a form (the gate fails). Such a form must use ConfirmDialog with submitsForm, because ConfirmModal has no guard. Overrule: add the same guard to ConfirmModal if a future design needs that shape.

ENGINE FACTS, READ FROM SOURCE ON 2026-10-07 (WebFetch of each engine's main): Chromium html_form_element.cc SubmitImplicitly: the first submit control decides; disabled means 'not activated; no implicit submission'; no layout check; with no button, submits when exactly one field can trigger. WebKit HTMLFormElement::submitImplicitly: clicks the first SUCCESSFUL submit button, skips disabled ones and keeps counting canTriggerImplicitSubmission(), which is just isTextField(), then submits when the count is 1. Firefox HTMLInputElement::MaybeSubmitForm: clicks the default submit element if one exists, else submits unless ImplicitSubmissionIsDisabled(). Side note, outside my touch list: modal.tsx:660-662 says 'a disabled submit button stops an implicit submission outright'. That is false in WebKit. ConfirmModal's hard gate stays safe because its onSubmit re-checks `armed && !loading`. I didn't change it.

REACT/NEXT FACTS VERIFIED in node_modules. react-dom 19.2.5 (react-dom-client.production.js:12129-12203): a submit whose native event is defaultPrevented skips the function action, but if `currentEventTransitionLane !== 0` it still calls startHostTransition(..., null), a pending form status with no action. Next 16.2.4's callServer wraps the dispatch in startTransition (app-call-server.js:14-16), and the App Router's root container is document (app-index.js:32, :293). So when Enter opens the withdraw dialog, its onOpen payee lookup would leave useFormStatus().pending stuck true for the length of the lookup. That is why the guard calls stopPropagation as well: React's root never sees a refused submit.

WHY THE onSubmit GUARD LIVES IN ConfirmDialog, NOT ON EACH <form>: the withdraw <form> is in a server component, where React event props can't be attached. One opt-in, native listener on the trigger's own form (found as the hidden default button's .form) covers server and client forms alike, through the trigger's own openGuard/onOpen path. date-select.tsx:159-166 already uses the same idiom (form.addEventListener('submit')). It is opt-in, so the ~40 other ConfirmDialog consumers render byte-identical markup (§2.4 pins this).
